raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
MoRI's auto dispatch picks the wire format from the expert weight dtype alone,
which does not say what the receiving kernel consumes. MXFP4 weights run a16w4,
a8w4 or a4w4 depending on the activation, gate mode, arch and token count; and
fp8 activations have two formats that share a payload but not a scale layout.

Ask AITER instead, through `resolve_activation_dtype()` (ROCm/aiter#5221), and
pass the quant type alongside the weight dtype so those two stay apart.
AITER owns the kernel dtype decision; an AITER without that API dispatches bf16
and warns.

| quant type | AITER consumes | dispatch | scales |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| per_1x128 | fp8 | fp8 | fp32 per 128 |
| per_1x32 | fp8 | **mxfp8** | e8m0 per 32 |
| per_1x32 | fp4x2 | fp4 | e8m0 per 32 |
| anything else, or an answer that depends on M | — | bf16 | — |

`per_Token` lands in the last row on purpose: MoRI has no per-token fp8 format.

On DeepSeek-V4-Pro the MoE is a8w4. Selecting mxfp8 dispatch matches the
activation format consumed by AITER and avoids an unnecessary
`upscale_mxfp4` plus re-quantization on the receive side.

The selection applies to the shared MoRI EPv1/EPv2 dispatcher and follows the
layer's activation and gate layout. Execution-kernel
`DISPATCHER_QUANT_CONFIG` overrides, explicit dispatch overrides, and the
existing combine selection are preserved.

## Why the answer is so often bf16

A dispatch format is fixed when the all-to-all buffers are sized — before any
token exists — while AITER's answer may depend on M. So M is not passed, and
AITER returns None wherever it would have been needed.

The two directions are not symmetric. Sending bf16 when AITER wanted fp8 costs
a quantize on the receive side. Sending a quantized format when the kernel
expects bf16 can cause a kernel-dispatch failure or incorrect output.
Unknown or batch-dependent answers therefore fall back to bf16.

`AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND` is a common reason M matters. For the interleaved
SwiGLU path, its default of 256 allows bf16 activations for small batches,
so auto must fall back to bf16. Setting it to 0 pins fp8 for every M and allows
mxfp8 dispatch. That fallback warns and names the variable; fallbacks that
follow from the hardware stay at info.

MXFP8 dispatch also requires AITER to both emit group-32 e8m0 scales and consume
them through the receive-side passthrough. If either capability is missing,
auto falls back to bf16.

## Validation

Validated on **8× MI355X** with
`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261028` and AITER
`285579b6211b0da30f35b91a890c29c823597cd1`:

- Full local pre-commit checks passed.
- AITER MXFP8 passthrough numerical tests: **3 passed**.
- Eight-rank MoRI EPv2 identity round trips with **automatic bf16, fp8, fp4,
  and mxfp8** selection: all passed
  (64 tokens/rank, hidden size 7168, top-k 6).
- SGLang AITER runner at **1, 8, and 112 tokens**: automatic mxfp8 output was
  **bit-identical** to bf16 input followed by internal quantization.
  The batch-dependent bf16 fallback was also exercised.
- Missing resolution API, missing MXFP8 receive capability, absent numerics,
  and separated-gate fallback checks passed.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, TP8 / DP8 attention / EP8 / MoRI EPv2**:
  all ranks automatically selected mxfp8; startup and decode CUDA graph
  capture succeeded. **17 completion requests**, including eight-way
  concurrency, returned the expected leading arithmetic answer and completed
  32 generated tokens each.

The model requests validate serving functionality; they are not a full
accuracy or performance benchmark.

## Related

- #36119 introduced `DispatchDtype.mxfp8` and the receive-side handling.
- ROCm/aiter#4954 provides the MXFP8 receive-side passthrough.
- ROCm/aiter#5221 exposes `resolve_activation_dtype()`.

nodes.body:
### PR Pundit review

(Testing PR Pundit Code Review agent. Not all comments may be relevant. This is a one-time automated pass: please address what is useful, no need to request a re-review. A quick reply per point (useful or not, and why) helps us calibrate the agent. Reach out to @peymanr for suggestions and feedback.)

| # | | Finding | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 🟠 | mxfp8 dispatch silently degrades to bf16 if aiter source grep breaks: this PR added source-text probe | `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/moriep.py:141-151` |
| 2 | 🟠 | mxfp8/bf16 fallback warning names wrong cause and bound variable: this PR left override text stale and hard-coded labels | `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py:499` |
| 3 | 🟠 | Outdated AITER silently drops MoRI dispatch from fp8/fp4 to bf16: this PR replaced the static mapping with resolve_activation_dtype | `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py:909-942` |
| 4 | 🟠 | No tests cover the new MoRI dispatch-format decision logic: this PR added it without tests | `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py:439-443` |

#### 1. 🟠 Should fix: mxfp8 dispatch silently degrades to bf16 if aiter source grep breaks: this PR added source-text probe
`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/moriep.py:141-151`

The new `can_consume` check in `_aiter_supports_mxfp8_dispatch` searches `inspect.getsource(aiter.fused_moe)` for the literal `hidden_states.dtype == dtypes.fp8 and a1_scale is not None`. If aiter rewords that line, or is installed without `.py` sources (`getsource` then raises `OSError`), the broad `except Exception` returns False and mxfp8 dispatch falls back to bf16, including under `SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=mxfp8`. A warning is logged, but the override's message only blames missing `scale_type`, so it misdiagnoses a failed source check. Prefer a feature/attribute or version probe and log which probe failed.

**Who is affected:** MoRI EP users with mxfp8 (a8w4) MoE on an aiter whose fused_moe source is reformatted or not shipped as .py.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

#### 2. 🟠 Should fix: mxfp8/bf16 fallback warning names wrong cause and bound variable: this PR left override text stale and hard-coded labels
`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py:499`

`_aiter_supports_mxfp8_dispatch` now requires both emit (`scale_type`) and consume (fused_moe fp8+`a1_scale`, ROCm/aiter#4954) sides, but the `SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=mxfp8` fallback warning in `_apply_dispatch_dtype_override` still blames only the missing `scale_type` emit side, misdiagnosing aiter that can emit but not consume. The new auto-path message hard-codes `(a8w4)` though `use_mxfp8` fp8-weight layers also reach it, and the None-dtype fallback always advises `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0`, which has no effect for per_1x32 MXFP4 Swiglu/SEPARATED layers decided by `GPTOSS_SWIGLU_MXFP4_BF16_BOUND`. Dispatch behaviour is correct; align the message text and name the bound that actually applies.

**Who is affected:** Operators of MXFP4 Swiglu-OAI MoE models with SEPARATED gate layout under MoRI EP on gfx950 who follow the warning's advice.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**Related past reviews:** [#17012](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17012) on `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/moriep.py`

#### 3. 🟠 Should fix: Outdated AITER silently drops MoRI dispatch from fp8/fp4 to bf16: this PR replaced the static mapping with resolve_activation_dtype
`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py:909-942`

When AITER lacks `resolve_activation_dtype` (builds older than ROCm/aiter#5221, Sep 2026), `resolve_aiter_dispatch_format` returns BF16 for every layer. MoRI then dispatches bf16 where the base sent fp8 (per_128x128 fp8) or fp4 (MXFP4), about 2x-4x the all-to-all bytes. The pinned `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` (285579b6) and the shipped image already include the API, so default builds are unaffected. The fallback is logged through `warning_once` with an upgrade hint. Keeping the old `weight_dtype` mapping for the M-independent fp8-block and plain-mxfp4 cases would avoid even this.

**Who is affected:** MoRI EP users of fp8 block-quant or MXFP4 MoE models who run an AITER build older than ROCm/aiter#5221 (not the pinned one).

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

#### 4. 🟠 Should fix: No tests cover the new MoRI dispatch-format decision logic: this PR added it without tests
`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py:439-443`

This PR adds no tests for the new dispatch-format selection: `resolve_aiter_dispatch_format`, its `wire_format` table, `_resolve_dispatch_dtype` with the mxfp8 → bf16 fallback, the `can_consume` probe, `build_dispatcher_quant_config` and `Fp8MoEMethod._aiter_moe_quant_type`. This logic picks the MoRI wire format. It also deliberately changes defaults: per-token fp8, and quant configs that report no `quant_type`, now dispatch bf16 instead of fp8. CPU unit tests with a stubbed `resolve_activation_dtype` are needed for each (quant_type, dtype) pair, the `None` and missing-API cases, the bound and None case, and the mxfp8 probe fallback; they would pin this behaviour.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers changing the MoRI/AITER dispatch selection; regressions in it would not be caught by CI.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**Related past reviews:** [#38546](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38546) on `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_glm53_flash_quark_moe.py`

<sub>Shared from a pilot of [PR Pundit](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/pr_pundit), an agentic code reviewer that builds and tests the change and reads the project's past reviews. Reviewed at `9078f17e`; findings checked and posted by @peymanr; points already raised on this PR are left out.</sub>

files.patch:
@@ -3,9 +3,10 @@
 import functools
 import inspect
 import logging
+import os
 from dataclasses import dataclass
 from enum import Enum
-from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Optional, Union
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, NamedTuple, Optional, Union
 
 import torch
 
@@ -394,6 +395,127 @@ def _is_mori_dispatch_output(dispatch_output: Any) -> bool:
     return hasattr(dispatch_output, "origin_topk_ids")
 
 
+class AiterDispatchFormat(str, Enum):
+    """What the dispatcher should send, i.e. what AITER's MoE will consume.
+    BF16 doubles as "unknown": the receive path always accepts it."""
+
+    FP8 = "fp8"  # fp8 + fp32 scale per 128
+    MXFP8 = "mxfp8"  # fp8 + e8m0 scale per 32
+    MXFP4 = "mxfp4"  # fp4x2 + e8m0 scale per 32
+    BF16 = "bf16"
+
+
+class AiterDispatchChoice(NamedTuple):
+    format: AiterDispatchFormat
+    reason: str
+    # Worth a warning: config can lift it. The rest follow from hardware or model.
+    actionable: bool = False
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _aiter_dispatch_dtype_api():
+    """AITER's `resolve_activation_dtype`, on builds that expose it."""
+    try:
+        from aiter import dtypes
+        from aiter.fused_moe import resolve_activation_dtype
+        from aiter.ops.flydsl.moe_common import GateMode
+    except ImportError:
+        return None
+
+    # (quant type, dtype AITER resolves to) -> wire format. Both fp8 rows carry
+    # the same payload and differ only in scale layout, which is why the quant
+    # type has to be part of the key. Both fp8 variants appear because AITER
+    # returns the weight dtype itself for per_1x128. Anything absent -- per_Token
+    # fp8 above all -- has no MoRI format.
+    fp8 = (torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.float8_e4m3fnuz)
+    wire_format = {
+        **{(AiterQuantType.PER_128X128, d): AiterDispatchFormat.FP8 for d in fp8},
+        **{(AiterQuantType.PER_1X32, d): AiterDispatchFormat.MXFP8 for d in fp8},
+        (AiterQuantType.PER_1X32, dtypes.fp4x2): AiterDispatchFormat.MXFP4,
+    }
+    return resolve_activation_dtype, GateMode, dtypes.bf16, wire_format
+
+
+def resolve_aiter_dispatch_format(
+    quant_type: Optional[AiterQuantType],
+    weight_dtype: Optional[torch.dtype],
+    runner_config: Optional[MoeRunnerConfig] = None,
+    swiglu_limit: Optional[float] = None,
+    gate_up_interleaved: Optional[bool] = None,
+    use_mxfp8: bool = False,
+) -> AiterDispatchChoice:
+    """Which activation format AITER's fused_moe will consume for this layer.
+
+    AITER's answer can depend on the token count M, but a dispatch format is
+    fixed when the all-to-all buffers are sized, so M is not passed and AITER
+    returns None wherever it would have mattered. Anything not committed to a
+    format answers BF16, which the receive path always accepts.
+    """
+    if quant_type is None or weight_dtype is None:
+        return AiterDispatchChoice(
+            AiterDispatchFormat.BF16, "quant method did not report the MoE numerics"
+        )
+
+    api = _aiter_dispatch_dtype_api()
+    if api is None:
+        return AiterDispatchChoice(
+            AiterDispatchFormat.BF16,
+            "AITER does not expose resolve_activation_dtype; upgrade it to let "
+            "the dispatch format follow what the MoE consumes",
+            actionable=True,
+        )
+    resolve_activation_dtype, GateMode, aiter_bf16, wire_format = api
+
+    if runner_config is None:
+        return AiterDispatchChoice(
+            AiterDispatchFormat.BF16, "quant method did not report the runner config"
+        )
+    swiglu_limit = aiter_swiglu_oai_limit(runner_config) or swiglu_limit or 0.0
+    interleave = (
+        bool(swiglu_limit > 0)
+        and (not is_gfx95_supported() or runner_config.gate_up_interleaved)
+        and envs.SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV.get()
+    )
+    if gate_up_interleaved is not None:
+        interleave = gate_up_interleaved
+    if runner_config.activation == "situ":
+        interleave = False
+
+    activation = _aiter_activation(runner_config)
+    if use_mxfp8 and is_gfx95_supported():
+        from aiter import ActivationType
+
+        activation = ActivationType.Swiglu
+
+    q_dtype_a = resolve_activation_dtype(
+        _aiter_quant_type(quant_type),
+        weight_dtype,
+        activation=activation,
+        gate_mode=GateMode.INTERLEAVE if interleave else GateMode.SEPARATED,
+    )
+    if q_dtype_a is None:
+        # bf16 where fp8 was wanted costs a quantize on the receive side; fp8
+        # where bf16 was wanted raises, or returns garbage at small M.
+        bound = int(os.getenv("AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND", "256"))
+        return AiterDispatchChoice(
+            AiterDispatchFormat.BF16,
+            "MoE activation dtype varies with batch size and a dispatch format "
+            f"cannot (AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND={bound}); set it to 0 to pin fp8 "
+            "and allow mxfp8 dispatch",
+            actionable=True,
+        )
+    if q_dtype_a == aiter_bf16:
+        return AiterDispatchChoice(AiterDispatchFormat.BF16, "MoE consumes bf16")
+
+    fmt = wire_format.get((quant_type, q_dtype_a))
+    if fmt is None:
+        return AiterDispatchChoice(
+            AiterDispatchFormat.BF16,
+            f"no MoRI wire format carries {q_dtype_a} for {quant_type.value}",
+        )
+    return AiterDispatchChoice(fmt, f"MoE consumes {q_dtype_a} ({quant_type.value})")
+
+
 def _resolve_mori_quant_type(
     dispatch_a1_dtype: torch.dtype,
     dispatch_scale: Optional[torch.Tensor],

@@ -437,3 +437,27 @@ def set_overlap_args(
     def clear_overlap_args(self) -> None:
         self.overlap_args = None
         self.meta_overlap_args = None
+
+
+def build_dispatcher_quant_config(
+    layer: torch.nn.Module,
+    weight_dtype: Optional[torch.dtype],
+    quant_type: Optional[Any] = None,
+    gate_up_interleaved: Optional[bool] = None,
+) -> dict:
+    """Describe a MoE layer's numerics to its dispatcher.
+
+    ``quant_type`` is the ``AiterQuantType`` the layer will hand AITER; it is
+    what separates the two fp8 activation formats. ``weight_dtype`` is semantic,
+    not storage: MXFP4 is stored as uint8 but reported as float4_e2m1fn_x2.
+    Consumers must tolerate every key but ``weight_dtype`` being absent.
+    """
+    runner_config = getattr(layer, "moe_runner_config", None)
+    return {
+        "weight_dtype": weight_dtype,
+        "quant_type": quant_type,
+        "runner_config": runner_config,
+        "gate_up_interleaved": gate_up_interleaved,
+        "swiglu_limit": getattr(runner_config, "swiglu_limit", None)
+        or getattr(runner_config, "gemm1_clamp_limit", None),
+    }

@@ -128,23 +128,27 @@ def _record_local_expert_count(local_expert_count: torch.Tensor) -> None:
 
 @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
 def _aiter_supports_mxfp8_dispatch() -> bool:
-    """Whether this aiter can consume fp8 activations with group-32 e8m0 scales.
+    """Can this aiter both emit and consume mxfp8 activations?
 
-    Probed rather than assumed, because the failure is silent in the worst way:
-    an older per_1x32 quant still returns fp8, but with continuous fp32 scales,
-    which the MoE then reads as e8m0 bytes and produces garbage rather than an
-    exception. Checking the signature keeps this a startup-time fallback instead
-    of a runtime corruption.
+    The halves ship in different commits (ROCm/aiter#4954 is the receive side),
+    and on a build with only the first the activations reach a bf16-only
+    quantizer and abort. No capability flag exists, hence the probes.
     """
     try:
         import inspect
 
+        import aiter.fused_moe as aiter_fused_moe
         from aiter import get_hip_quant
 
-        return "scale_type" in inspect.signature(get_hip_quant).parameters or any(
+        can_emit = "scale_type" in inspect.signature(get_hip_quant).parameters or any(
             "scale_type" in inspect.signature(f).parameters
             for f in (get_hip_quant(QuantType.per_1x32),)
         )
+        can_consume = (
+            "hidden_states.dtype == dtypes.fp8 and a1_scale is not None"
+            in inspect.getsource(aiter_fused_moe)
+        )
+        return can_emit and can_consume
     except Exception:
         return False
 
@@ -896,16 +900,47 @@ def combine_b(self, *args, **kwargs):
     def set_quant_config(self, quant_config: dict) -> None:
         self.quant_config = quant_config
         weight_dtype = quant_config.get("weight_dtype")
-        self.dispatch_dtype = DispatchDtype.bf16
-        if weight_dtype == torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2:
-            self.dispatch_dtype = DispatchDtype.fp4
-        elif weight_dtype in (torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.float8_e4m3fnuz):
-            self.dispatch_dtype = DispatchDtype.fp8
+        self.dispatch_dtype = self._resolve_dispatch_dtype(quant_config)
         self.combine_dtype = self._default_combine_dtype(weight_dtype)
         # Combine overrides read the final dispatch dtype, so apply dispatch first.
         self._apply_dispatch_dtype_override()
         self._apply_combine_dtype_override()
 
+    def _resolve_dispatch_dtype(self, quant_config: dict) -> DispatchDtype:
+        """Pick the wire format from the activation dtype the MoE consumes."""
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.moe_runner.aiter import (
+            AiterDispatchFormat,
+            resolve_aiter_dispatch_format,
+        )
+
+        choice = resolve_aiter_dispatch_format(
+            quant_config.get("quant_type"),
+            quant_config.get("weight_dtype"),
+            runner_config=quant_config.get("runner_config"),
+            use_mxfp8=quant_config.get("use_mxfp8", False),

### PR Pundit review

(Testing PR Pundit Code Review agent. Not all comments may be relevant. This is a one-time automated pass: please address what is useful, no need to request a re-review. A quick reply per point (useful or not, and why) helps us calibrate the agent. Reach out to @peymanr for suggestions and feedback.)

| # | | Finding | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 🟠 | mxfp8 dispatch silently degrades to bf16 if aiter source grep breaks: this PR added source-text probe | `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/moriep.py:141-151` |
| 2 | 🟠 | mxfp8/bf16 fallback warning names wrong cause and bound variable: this PR left override text stale and hard-coded labels | `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py:499` |
| 3 | 🟠 | Outdated AITER silently drops MoRI dispatch from fp8/fp4 to bf16: this PR replaced the static mapping with resolve_activation_dtype | `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py:909-942` |
| 4 | 🟠 | No tests cover the new MoRI dispatch-format decision logic: this PR added it without tests | `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py:439-443` |

#### 1. 🟠 Should fix: mxfp8 dispatch silently degrades to bf16 if aiter source grep breaks: this PR added source-text probe
`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/moriep.py:141-151`

The new `can_consume` check in `_aiter_supports_mxfp8_dispatch` searches `inspect.getsource(aiter.fused_moe)` for the literal `hidden_states.dtype == dtypes.fp8 and a1_scale is not None`. If aiter rewords that line, or is installed without `.py` sources (`getsource` then raises `OSError`), the broad `except Exception` returns False and mxfp8 dispatch falls back to bf16, including under `SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=mxfp8`. A warning is logged, but the override's message only blames missing `scale_type`, so it misdiagnoses a failed source check. Prefer a feature/attribute or version probe and log which probe failed.

**Who is affected:** MoRI EP users with mxfp8 (a8w4) MoE on an aiter whose fused_moe source is reformatted or not shipped as .py.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

#### 2. 🟠 Should fix: mxfp8/bf16 fallback warning names wrong cause and bound variable: this PR left override text stale and hard-coded labels
`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py:499`

`_aiter_supports_mxfp8_dispatch` now requires both emit (`scale_type`) and consume (fused_moe fp8+`a1_scale`, ROCm/aiter#4954) sides, but the `SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=mxfp8` fallback warning in `_apply_dispatch_dtype_override` still blames only the missing `scale_type` emit side, misdiagnosing aiter that can emit but not consume. The new auto-path message hard-codes `(a8w4)` though `use_mxfp8` fp8-weight layers also reach it, and the None-dtype fallback always advises `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0`, which has no effect for per_1x32 MXFP4 Swiglu/SEPARATED layers decided by `GPTOSS_SWIGLU_MXFP4_BF16_BOUND`. Dispatch behaviour is correct; align the message text and name the bound that actually applies.

**Who is affected:** Operators of MXFP4 Swiglu-OAI MoE models with SEPARATED gate layout under MoRI EP on gfx950 who follow the warning's advice.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**Related past reviews:** [#17012](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17012) on `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/moriep.py`

#### 3. 🟠 Should fix: Outdated AITER silently drops MoRI dispatch from fp8/fp4 to bf16: this PR replaced the static mapping with resolve_activation_dtype
`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py:909-942`

When AITER lacks `resolve_activation_dtype` (builds older than ROCm/aiter#5221, Sep 2026), `resolve_aiter_dispatch_format` returns BF16 for every layer. MoRI then dispatches bf16 where the base sent fp8 (per_128x128 fp8) or fp4 (MXFP4), about 2x-4x the all-to-all bytes. The pinned `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` (285579b6) and the shipped image already include the API, so default builds are unaffected. The fallback is logged through `warning_once` with an upgrade hint. Keeping the old `weight_dtype` mapping for the M-independent fp8-block and plain-mxfp4 cases would avoid even this.

**Who is affected:** MoRI EP users of fp8 block-quant or MXFP4 MoE models who run an AITER build older than ROCm/aiter#5221 (not the pinned one).

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

#### 4. 🟠 Should fix: No tests cover the new MoRI dispatch-format decision logic: this PR added it without tests
`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py:439-443`

This PR adds no tests for the new dispatch-format selection: `resolve_aiter_dispatch_format`, its `wire_format` table, `_resolve_dispatch_dtype` with the mxfp8 → bf16 fallback, the `can_consume` probe, `build_dispatcher_quant_config` and `Fp8MoEMethod._aiter_moe_quant_type`. This logic picks the MoRI wire format. It also deliberately changes defaults: per-token fp8, and quant configs that report no `quant_type`, now dispatch bf16 instead of fp8. CPU unit tests with a stubbed `resolve_activation_dtype` are needed for each (quant_type, dtype) pair, the `None` and missing-API cases, the bound and None case, and the mxfp8 probe fallback; they would pin this behaviour.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers changing the MoRI/AITER dispatch selection; regressions in it would not be caught by CI.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**Related past reviews:** [#38546](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38546) on `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_glm53_flash_quark_moe.py`
